# Ting 0.7.5
## New
- **Links in micro-app results.** Markdown output (`output.as: markdown`) now shows `[text](target)` links. The target is an `http`, `https` or `mailto` URL, a `file` URL or an absolute path (`/…` or `~/…`); a target with spaces is written as `[text](<~/My Folder>)`. A click opens a web or mail link, opens a folder in Finder, and shows any other file selected in Finder. A file link never opens the file itself, so a result from the web or an AI cannot start a script or an app. Other targets stay plain text. - Links are underlined. A web or mail link has the link colour; a file link keeps the colour of the text around it, with a faint underline, so a list of files stays readable. - The first click on a link shows a warning in the result panel: a link comes from the micro-app's output, which can carry text from the web or an AI, and may lead to a harmful site. The warning shows where the link goes. **Open Link** (Return) follows it and the warning does not show again; **Cancel** (Esc) closes the warning and leaves the result open. - **Links in a monospaced tree.** A code block fenced as ```` ```links ```` keeps its monospaced lines, so a `├──` tree stays aligned, and its links work. See [the format](../micro-apps/FORMAT.md). - **A converter in launcha.** Next to the calculator, launcha converts units (`5 yd to m`, `100 f in c`, `60 mph to km/h`), number bases (`255 to hex`, `0xff`), Unix time (`1700000000 to date`, `now to unix`) and dates (`now + 2 days`, `3 days ago`, `2026-12-25 - today`). The value comes first and `Return` copies it. Ting converts with the units and calendar of macOS; US and imperial units use their exact legal factors. Turn it off with **Convert in launcha** in Settings › General, or with `"converter": false` under `launcha`. - **Global shortcuts for apps.** Select an app in launcha and press `⌘⇧K` to record a shortcut that opens that exact app bundle. Saving replaces the app's previous shortcut and, after confirmation, any other app's assignment to the same keys. The leader and launcha shortcuts stay protected. Shortcuts appear on app rows and can be changed or removed from the row's menu.
## Fix
- The release scripts build and check with the Xcode 27 toolchain. `package_app.sh` builds with the native build system, and `release.sh` checks one architecture per `lipo` call, as the newer `lipo` refuses several after `-verify_arch`. The service tests find `Sparkle.framework` under Swift Build again.
## Upgrade
A downloaded copy: choose **Check for Updates…** in Ting. A Homebrew copy: choose **Update Ting via Homebrew…** in Ting's menu. Settings, bindings, micro-apps and permissions are preserved. Requires macOS 14 or later; the signed, notarized and stapled universal app supports Apple Silicon and Intel.
